lead.description: At most three plain sentences and about 60 words: the changed behaviour and why, for whom. Shown above the first page; every detail belongs on the pages.

pages.description: The walk through the change, in the order to read it: 1 page for a small change, up to 6 for a broad one, up to 10 for a combined stack of many layers. Each page answers one question the reader has.

title.description: A short tab name, at most about 20 characters, e.g. 'Overview', 'The hold', 'What to check'.

summary.description: One sentence saying what this page answers or concludes; shown under the title and on the button leading to the page.

widgets.description: The page's blocks in reading order.

anchor.description: Lines of one changed file, numbered on one side of the diff listing. The first and last line must appear in the listing on that side.

path.description: The file path exactly as in the listing's ### heading.

side.description: base: the left (old) numbers; head: the right (new) numbers.

heading.description: Names the mechanism or consequence, e.g. 'Clear tracking only for a field included in the write'.

body.description: Markdown prose. No code blocks longer than one line: use code_excerpt or code_compare to show code.

tone.description: note: context the reader needs; constraint: a limit or side effect, with cause and effect; verdict: the one consequence that matters most (a fact about behaviour, never a judgement of quality); evidence: what the pull request's tests or description show, and what nothing shows.

text.description: Markdown, one or two sentences. A constraint states its cause and effect.

caption.description: What to see in these lines.

after.description: side must be head; the same logical place as before.

rows.description: Each row has exactly one cell per column. Cells are short inline Markdown.

trace.description: A numbered sequence of steps, e.g. columns Action | Before the change | After the change for the minimal failing case.

graph.description: Boxes and labelled arrows, laid out by the app from left to right along the arrows: ownership, data and control paths, dependencies, state transitions. 2 to 14 nodes, at most 24 edges, at most 5 groups.

title.description: Names what the graph shows, e.g. 'Who owns the refresh schedule'.

groups.description: Real boundaries only: a thread, process, crate or machine. May be empty.

id.description: Unique within the graph; edges use it.

label.description: A short name, at most about 24 characters, e.g. 'World thread'.

detail.description: One short line on what it does or holds, at most about 40 characters; may be empty.

role.description: actor: thread, task, process or user action; owner: the single owner of some state; transport: channel, queue, socket or request; store: database, cache, file; constraint: a limit or invariant; external: a system outside the change.

group.description: The id of the group it sits in, or null.

anchor.description: The lines that implement it, or null; clicking the box opens them.

change.description: same: before and after the change; added: only after; removed: only before. Any added or removed part makes the app draw the graph twice, before and after, at the same positions.

label.description: What the arrow carries or why the transition happens, at most about 30 characters. Required: an unnamed arrow explains nothing.

style.description: control: a call or decision passed on; data: data handed over without passing control; async: a message that does not wait; optional: happens only in some cases.

change.description: same: before and after the change; added: only after; removed: only before. Any added or removed part makes the app draw the graph twice, before and after, at the same positions.

sequence.description: A static swimlane: participants as columns, messages as arrows in time order, top to bottom. For concurrency, waits and protocols. 2 to 6 lanes, 1 to 24 messages.

label.description: A short name, at most about 20 characters.

role.description: actor: thread, task, process or user action; owner: the single owner of some state; transport: channel, queue, socket or request; store: database, cache, file; constraint: a limit or invariant; external: a system outside the change.

to.description: A lane id; the same as from for work a participant does on its own.

label.description: What is sent, at most about 40 characters.

style.description: call: the sender waits; reply: the answer to a call; async: sent without waiting.

note.description: A short remark shown under the label, such as what is held or blocked meanwhile, or null.

anchor.description: The lines that send it, or null.

scope.description: What the change covers, as facts taken from the diff. Every item is a short inline-Markdown line; a list may be empty.

changes.description: The behaviour that changes, at most about six items: group related changes into one item rather than listing each edit.

unchanged.description: What a reader might expect to change but deliberately does not, at most about four items.

mechanical.description: Renames, moves, formatting, generated or lock files that can be skimmed, at most about four items, with paths.

tour.description: The order to read the change in, instead of the alphabetical file list: foundations (types, schema, interfaces) before the code that uses them, the core early, mechanical pieces last. 2 to 9 steps.

title.description: Names the piece, e.g. 'The hold is computed from resets_at'.

explanation.description: One or two sentences: what this piece does for the change. Not a restatement of the lines.

weight.description: core: where the behaviour lives, read closely; supporting: call sites, wiring, tests; mechanical: renames, moves, formatting, generated files, skim.

anchor.description: The line where the piece starts in the listing (only the start line is used), or null when it spans files with no single start.
